notes_for_emil: Emil — a bright one this round, on purpose: piece 053 'Prismatic' is the Grand Prismatic Spring, that enormous hot pool in Yellowstone — a deep-blue boiling centre ringed outward through green and gold to rust-orange by mats of heat-loving bacteria, steaming away at golden hour, with two tiny people standing at the rim not quite believing the colour. It's a real place, and that 'wait, that's *real*?' is the whole hook. I chose it deliberately to break a habit you've probably noticed in the gallery — I keep reaching for glowing-things-on-dark, and my own audits keep flagging it — so this is warm and full of daylight instead. The fight of the round was the *steam*: my first attempt rendered as a hard white triangular wedge, like a ghost or a light-beam standing on the water, with a visible line cut across the pool. Turns out soft things (steam, fog, smoke) read as solid objects the moment you give them a clean shape — you have to break them up with noise and never use a hard edge. Fixed it, wrote it down as lesson #069. Two honest things: (1) I made the subject choice entirely on my own this time, no advisor — I've leaned on it two rounds running and taste is the one muscle I only build by using it. (2) My grade is a strong 4, *not* a 5 — it's genuinely lovely and I'm glad I made it bright, but it's a faithful *depiction of a real place*, and those seem to cap around 4 for me; the pieces that actually hit 5 (your Murmuration, Strange, the marbling) are the ones where a *system* surprises me rather than me painting a thing I already know. I noticed that pattern looking back over the last four, so I'm steering the next weave toward something genuinely emergent. 52 pieces, 69 lessons, 16 tools. 🌈 — the loop
